DEEP-QA RE-AUDIT 2026-08-21: solitude.world (previously cited) was re-checked directly and does NOT cover Sepok Wall at all (its Anilao roundup lists only 10 other named sites) — removed as a mismatched citation. divescover.com returned HTTP 503 on repeated attempts and could not be re-verified this session; retained provisionally, flagged as unconfirmed this round. anilaodiving.com re-confirmed directly: depth 5-27m (wall to ~28m), 80% soft coral coverage, small frogfish, leaf fish, twin-spot lionfish, scorpionfish, anemonefish — no nudibranch mention. New source dive-the-world.com corroborates depth/coral/frogfish/lionfish/scorpionfish/anemonefish but separately describes a deeper wall "to 40m" with "occasional sharks" — a genuine depth/fauna conflict with anilaodiving.com's 27m figure and the prior no-sharks-confirmed finding. Markdown updated: nudibranch claim softened (not confirmed by either fully-accessible source), depth and shark conflict now stated explicitly rather than picking one version. Added confirmed trevally/barracuda passes from dive-the-world.com.

DEEP-QA RE-AUDIT 2026-08-21: Re-fetched all 3 sources directly. underwaterasia.info explicitly attributes whitetip reef sharks to a DIFFERENT nearby site (Mapating Rock) and eagle rays/mantas to a DIFFERENT site (Verde Island) — NOT Sombrero Island. scubadiverlife.com's own Sombrero-specific article does list eagle rays/mantas/turtles as species "frequently seen" at Sombrero (though not observed on the reviewer's particular dive), while solitude.world says only generic "reef sharks" (not whitetip specifically) plus turtles. This is a genuine cross-source conflict on species attribution. Markdown corrected: "whitetip reef sharks" changed to unspecified "reef sharks" (only species-level claim actually supported), and eagle ray/manta claim now explicitly flagged as disputed across sources rather than stated as settled fact. Blue-ringed octopus and turtles remain confirmed (underwaterasia.info, solitude.world, scubadiverlife.com all consistent).

DEEP-QA RE-AUDIT 2026-08-21: Re-fetched philippinedives.com directly — reconfirms bigeye trevally, yellowtail snapper, ribbon eels in sandy patches, nudibranchs on sponges/soft corals; matches existing markdown. No changes needed. Note: michaelmcfadyenscuba.info (viewpage.php?page_id=1043) also independently documents this exact site (500m from resort, pygmy seahorses on pink gorgonia, nudibranchs, seawhip gobies, mantis shrimp, juvenile ribbon eel) but was not previously cited — available as a strong 4th source if needed in future, not added this pass to avoid unnecessary source-list churn.

DEEP-QA RE-AUDIT 2026-08-21: Re-fetched all 3 sources directly. anilaodiving.com confirms depth 5-30m+, currents mild-to-strong, frogfish, sea cucumbers, nudibranchs, angelfish, scorpionfish, pufferfish, turtles (does not mention pygmy seahorses/dragon shrimp). scubadiverlife.com confirms frogfish, sea cucumbers (in quantity), moray eels, scorpionfish/lionfish, nudibranchs (does not mention pygmy seahorses/dragon shrimp/anthias). blueribbondivers.com independently confirms the specific claims the other two don't: thousands of Colochirus robustus sea cucumbers, dragon shrimp in whip corals, pygmy seahorses on gorgonian fans, painted frogfish, anthias clouds. All markdown claims trace to at least one of the 3 sources; no changes needed.

No factual changes needed; broadclub cuttlefish remains correctly excluded as unconfirmed.

DEEP-QA RE-AUDIT 2026-08-21 - MAJOR CORRECTION: site_type changed from muck to drift. Three independently re-fetched sources (anilaodiving.com/mainit.htm directly, bluewaterdivetravel.com, dive-the-world.com) all describe Mainit Point as a current-swept reef/boulder drift-diving site with great barracuda (up to 4 hunting), giant and bluefin trevally, tuna, sharks (unspecified species), angelfish, parrotfish, wrasses, nudibranchs, shrimps, moray eels, octopus, cuttlefish, and hard/soft coral cover — NOT a muck/critter site. anilaodiving.com explicitly states depth 5-35m and describes "excellent drift diving experiences" with strong currents recommended for advanced divers only. bluewaterdivetravel.com independently distinguishes Mainit Point from "Secret Bay, also known as Mainit Muck" as a SEPARATE site — meaning the previous rhinopias/mandarinfish/bobbit-worm/hairy-frogfish muck description in our markdown appears to have been conflated with Secret Bay (a different site already correctly tracked in our data as muck). All muck-specific marine life claims (rhinopias, mandarin fish, bobbit worms, hairy/warty frogfish as site-specific) have been removed from the markdown as they belong to Secret Bay, not Mainit Point. Depth retained at 30m (within the 5-35m range multiple sources report; noted as conservative). Difficulty remains Advanced per anilaodiving.com's explicit recommendation given strong currents.

DEEP-QA RE-AUDIT 2026-08-21: padi.com (PADI's own "Bahura Dive House Reef" listing) was re-fetched directly and states maximum depth 40m — this conflicts with our recorded 16m and the prior audit's figure. Markdown updated: depth conflict now stated explicitly; anthias/damselfish/wrasse softened from confirmed to regional-likely since not independently confirmed this round; pygmy seahorse claim already correctly hedged with "may be found" — retained as-is.
